title: Break, then the Lafayette Theater
summary: Interview resumes in the 1920s; she played the Lafayette in Harlem with success and then went to Washington.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So do you feel like going on? You can stop, you know.
Yeah. I don't need to stop. I have nothing to do.
Okay. So tell me -- let's see, we've
covered -- we'll probably later go on back.
Yeah, back, because something else will come to me, uh-huh.
And I want you to tell me more about Mattie Hite Height and these various people.
So now we're up to New York. And the 1920's now. And you would be with "How Come". And you did some clubs and things here. Did you ever do the Lafayette Theater?
Yes. I played the Lafayette. And what band was there? It will come to me. I played the Lafayette. And I cleaned up at the Lafayette. Yes, thank God, I made good at the Lafayette.
And then I never worked at the other theaters. From the Lafayette I went to Washington. Did you see what band I worked with at the Lafayette?
I can only see what you did with records
